title: Tiered latency-credit SKUs and contractual failsafe for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Summary:
We will prototype a set of Dedicated Capacity SKUs that expose predictable low-latency "lanes" via a credit accounting model. Instead of only selling raw reserved GPU units or opaque "burst" windows, these SKUs sell baseline capacity + a bank of latency credits that are consumed when requests need to be placed into a guaranteed low-latency execution path. The goal is to give enterprise customers deterministic tail-latency guarantees while preserving economics for variable workloads and enabling clear contract language for failure modes and fallbacks.

Why this work:
- Customers repeatedly ask for contractual latency guarantees without wanting to overcommit GPU hours for the common case.
- Existing "burst" constructs are opaque and have led to support escalations when customers hit hidden preemption/overflow semantics.
- A credit-based SKU gives measurable consumption, straightforward pricing, and clear escalation/fallback behavior in contracts.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: SKU definitions, billing experiment matrix, contract language templates (SLA clauses + failsafe fallbacks), telemetry and metric definitions, console UX for credit balances, and an initial pilot with 2 enterprise customers. Also coordination with legal to draft terms for overflow/fallback.
- Non-goal: Replacing existing Reserved GPU commit models; this is an additive SKU targeted at latency-sensitive enterprise workloads that prefer predictable tail latency over absolute throughput pricing.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 SKUs (Gold/Silver/Bronze) with explicit baseline throughput, latency-credit earn/consume rules, and list pricing ranges for pilot customers.
Contract appendix language drafted describing fallback behavior (overflow to best-effort lane, automatic credit top-ups, preemptible fallbacks, and notification SLAs) and reviewed by Legal.
Billing prototype that can meter latency-credit consumption and generate a weekly consumption report; metrics surfaced in Console and available via CSV export.
Telemetry spec complete: how to measure credit consumption, per-request tagging, and SLO verification methodology (p90/p95/p99 tail-latency tied to credit budgets).
Pilot onboarding checklist and runbook documented; first pilot signed and instrumented with a single enterprise customer for 8-week trial.
tasks: Draft SKU definitions and price bands (PM) - include example workload trace billing simulation
Define credit accounting: how credits are charged per request (ENG + PM) - prototype meter in sandbox
Legal: draft SLA appendix and failure-mode language
Console: credit balance UI mockups and API contract for consumption readout (DES + ENG)
Billing: map metering events to billing pipeline and test invoice sample outputs
Pilot ops: onboarding playbook, support escalation matrix, rollback and cancellation terms
notes: Design thought: credit granularity should be per-model-per-seqlength band to avoid overcharging for short chat messages vs long generations.
Experimentation idea: offer a low-cost Silver SKU with higher p99 latency but large credit bank vs Gold with small bank and strict p99. Measure conversion and SLA grievance rates.
Risk: customers may try to game credits by sending many small requests; mitigation: minimum per-request charge and prefix caching discounts documented in billing spec.
Related artifacts: Confluence: /pages/dedicated/latency-credit-skus (PRD + simulations), Spreadsheet: latency-credit-sim-v1 (price elasticity sims).
